newsitem.title: CHINA: China's Jiang says Taiwan key to Sino-U.S. ties.
newsitem.headline: China's Jiang says Taiwan key to Sino-U.S. ties.

text.p: Chinese President Jiang Zemin described Sino-U.S. ties as being like "sunshine after rain" but said the United States must handle the sensitive issue of Taiwan with care, the People's Daily said on Saturday.

"We have noticed that more U.S. congressmen have realised the sensitiveness and importance of the Taiwan question," Jiang told visiting U.S. Speaker of the House of Representatives Newt Gingrich on Friday.
China and the United States are repairing ties strained by disputes that have ranged from human rights to trade and Taiwan.
U.S. Vice-President Al Gore wound up a visit to China on Friday as part of the effort to ensure relations remain healthy and to prepare for an exchange of presidential visits.
While ties between the United States and China were now like "sunshine after rain", Jiang called on Gingrich to help prevent the Taiwan issue from obstructing further improvement.
"The U.S. Congress has great influence in foreign affairs," Jiang was quoted as saying. "We hope Congress will play an active and constructive role in promoting bilateral relations."
Jiang, while reaching out to the U.S. administration, has also been courting U.S. congressmen, encouraging visits by congressional delegations visits.

Beijing was enraged by the 1995 visit to the United States by Taiwan President Lee Teng-hui, particularly since it had been assured by the U.S. administration that Lee would not be permitted to make the trip.
Congress pushed hard for clearance for Lee and the visit was allowed to proceed.
China and Taiwan have been rivals since the end of the Chinese civil war in 1949. Beijing views Taiwan as a renegade province and has tried to isolate it diplomatically.
Gingrich, who arrived in Beijing on Thursday with a bipartisan congressional delegation, is scheduled to make a brief stop in Taiwan before winding up his Asian tour.
